Improving database performance with Amazon
ElastiCache
While DynamoDB DAX provides idx_3703871c an in-memory caching solution for DynamoDB tables, you
may wonder about caching options for Amazon RDS.
Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service that can be used with Amazon RDS to
improve read performance by storing frequently accessed data in memory, reducing the need
to query the backend database directly.
Caching services such as ElastiCache improve read performance because your application does
not need to call the backend database to retrieve frequently accessed data. This also reduces
the load on your Amazon RDS instances.
AWS offers three in-memory caching engines: Valkey, Memcached, and Redis.
Redis is designed for idx_27ce0603 complex data structures and supports features such as Multi-AZ
deployment, data encryption, replication, and automatic failover
Memcached is optimized idx_d6d6e9c6 for simpler data types but supports large nodes with
multiple cores and threads, and it scales out effectively
Valkey is an open-source idx_01b74584 alternative to Redis. It can handle a variety of workloads,
such as caching, session stores, and message queues, and can act as a primary database
In the next section, you will learn about Amazon Redshift, which is designed for analytical
workloads.
Building data warehousing solutions with Amazon
Redshift
Data warehousing idx_0c833678 solutions like idx_bed66b86 Amazon Redshift are designed to help businesses pull data
from other relational databases or storage platforms and perform complex data analytics.
For example, you can combine data across customer orders, inventory systems, supplier
contacts and agreements, and financial data to analyze trends, demand, and return on
investment (ROI). Data warehousing solutions also help you idx_f4068324 build Business Intelligence (BI)
platforms, enabling business executives to make informed decisions.
•
•
•

Unlike Amazon RDS, which idx_44178b4c is an Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) solution, data
warehousing platforms like Amazon Redshift are idx_a41d9672 designed for Online Analytical Processing
(OLAP).
Instead of organizing data as rows—where each item is created and managed as a transaction
—Redshift uses a columnar storage format to analyze large datasets efficiently. It can scale
up to petabytes of data and idx_660fab8d supports massively parallel processing (MPP) for high-
performance querying.

Migrating databases with AWS Database Migration
Service
Amazon offers the Database Migration Service (DMS), which is commonly used to help
businesses idx_026cd73f migrate their idx_0e250933 on-premises databases to the AWS Cloud. You can migrate existing
databases to Amazon RDS, DynamoDB, or Redshift easily using a managed service that
handles all the heavy lifting for you.
You no longer need to perform a manual backup of your on-premises database and then restore
it in the cloud. This process usually results in a more extended outage period. Instead, with
AWS DMS, AWS helps you to configure a source endpoint for the source database and a target
endpoint for your target database. Using replication, the data and any changes are migrated
across to the target database. When you are ready to switch over, you simply point your
application to the new target database endpoint.
You can perform a one-time migration or even configure continuous replication to migrate
ongoing changes from your on-premises database over a defined period.
With AWS DMS, you can perform:
Homogeneous migrations, such as MySQL to MySQL or Oracle to Oracle
Heterogeneous migrations, such as Oracle to Microsoft SQL Server
For heterogeneous migrations, you must first use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS
SCT) to convert the idx_f3b3d3a5 schema of the destination cloud database before performing the
migration.
AWS DMS simplifies database migrations by reducing the complexity, risk, and downtime
traditionally associated with moving databases to the cloud. Whether you are migrating
between similar database engines or converting to a different database platform, AWS DMS
provides a managed solution that helps you transfer data securely and efficiently. By
combining AWS DMS with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool for heterogeneous migrations,
organizations can modernize their database environments and accelerate their cloud adoption
journey with minimal disruption to business operations.

Belly Brew Co. Limited. The database will be used to host customer contact information for its
upcoming marketing campaigns. As part of the website you will build using this study guide,
you will need to provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. This database will be used to
capture customer contact data, which the marketing team will find invaluable.

Chapter 9 270
Summary
In this chapter, you learned about various AWS database services available to support a wide
range of use cases. You discovered some fundamental differences between SQL and NoSQL
(Relational vs. Non-Relational) databases and their specific use cases.
Amazon RDS is a relational database service that supports various engines such as MySQL,
PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and Oracle. AWS also offers its own proprietary database
called Amazon Aurora, designed for enterprise-grade applications and offering a suite of
features to meet modern application requirements. Amazon Aurora provides six copies of the
database using a clustered storage solution spread across three Availability Zones and includes
advanced features such as self-healing capabilities.
You learned about the importance of designing your database solution for high availability
using multi-AZ deployments and for scaling read operations using read replicas. You also
learned about the importance of configuring both automatic and manual backups to mitigate
the impact of major disasters or data corruption issues.
You then learned how DynamoDB is particularly useful for cutting-edge mobile and web
applications, where applications require single-digit millisecond latency and data structures
need to be flexible without a strict schema. This NoSQL offering from AWS also includes
advanced features such as a built-in in-memory caching service called DynamoDB
Accelerator (DAX) and the ability to deploy a multi-master (multi-active) database solution
across multiple regions.
In addition, you learned about Amazon ElastiCache, which provides in-memory caching
engines such as Redis and Memcached. For data warehousing solutions, AWS offers the
Amazon Redshift service, available both as a provisioned cluster and as a serverless solution.
Amazon Redshift Spectrum also allows you to query data stored in Amazon S3 directly, without
having to import it into a Redshift cluster.
Finally, you learned about the AWS Database Migration Service (DMS), which enables
migration of on-premises databases using both homogeneous and heterogeneous migration
options. The latter requires the use of the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT). DMS supports
both one-time migrations and ongoing replication from a source database to a destination
database.
In the next chapter, we will learn how to make the application highly available, fault-tolerant,
and elastic using Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, AWS Secrets Manager, and Amazon SES.

High Availability, Fault Tolerance,
and Elasticity on AWS
Businesses strive to ensure that their software applications are always available and experience
minimal downtime. This is particularly critical when end customers need access to those
applications, such as customers of an e-commerce business. Any downtime can impact not
only sales but also the company's reputation. Therefore, designing solutions that are highly
available or even fault-tolerant is essential for most businesses.
If you deploy your application on a single EC2 instance supported by a single database
instance, you create a single point of failure. If there are idx_76295bc9 any hardware or software issues with
the EC2 instance, or if the Availability Zone in which it is deployed goes offline, your customers
will be unable to access the application. Modern architectural patterns, therefore, incorporate
high availability into their idx_1ee3d5fa design. This often involves having multiple EC2 instances serving
the same application, ideally deployed across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) within a
region.
Using the multi-AZ option for your Amazon RDS database is another example of avoiding
single points of failure. If your primary instance fails, AWS performs a failover to the standby
instance, which maintains an up-to-date copy of your data. Your RDS database remains highly
available, although there may be a few seconds of downtime during the failover process.
Fault tolerance takes this concept one idx_0520dfe0 step further, ensuring that your application continues
to operate even if a component fails. In this case, Amazon RDS Multi-AZ alone is insufficient, as
the failover process still introduces a brief period of downtime. Instead, you might re-architect
your solution to use DynamoDB Global Tables, which offer the level of fault tolerance required.
If a region goes offline, traffic can be redirected to another region with a copy of the DynamoDB
table, maintaining seamless access.
You also want your application to be scalable, ensuring you have sufficient resources to handle
changes in demand. You must be able to scale out as demand increases and scale in as it
decreases. Scaling out may involve adding more EC2 instances to your fleet and distributing
the load across the increased compute capacity. Conversely, when demand drops, you want to
scale back and terminate unused EC2 instances to reduce costs and avoid waste. This ability to
dynamically adjust resources in response to idx_e94b0be1 fluctuating demand is known as elasticity.

Designing for high availability with Elastic Load
Balancers
One way to ensure high availability is by hosting multiple resources that serve the same
application, such as several EC2 instances running the same web application. However, you
need a mechanism to distribute idx_d3b11b64 incoming customer traffic across these resources in a way that
ensures even load distribution across the fleet. This enables you to distribute incoming traffic
effectively and deliver a consistent experience for all users. Amazon Elastic Load Balancers
(ELBs) are designed for precisely this purpose.

Chapter 10 276
ELBs can distribute traffic across multiple EC2 instances, containers, IP addresses, and even
Lambda functions. If a particular EC2 instance fails, for example, the load balancer will redirect
traffic to other healthy instances in the fleet.
Amazon load balancers detect failed instances by performing health checks—ongoing checks
on instances and the applications running on them to verify they are healthy and responsive.
The load balancer only routes traffic to instances that pass these health checks, indicating they
are live and operational.
Amazon Elastic Load Balancers are regional services that can route traffic to resources across
multiple AZs within a region. You deploy your load balancer in a VPC and specify which AZs
will host your load balancer nodes. The following section explains how to deploy your load
balancer in a VPC.
But before exploring the different types of AWS Load Balancers, it's helpful to understand the
Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, which is a framework used to describe how data
travels across a network.
Overview of the OSI model
Published in 1984, the OSI model outlines the process idx_0fe3dda5 by which data flows through a network
system. The OSI model is divided idx_f3757a00 into seven layers, with each layer responsible for a specific
part of the network communication process and utilizing various protocols at that layer.
Different hardware and software components that enable data transfer operate at varying
layers of the OSI model. For example, packet-filtering firewalls, which inspect IP addresses,
ports, and transport layer protocols such as TCP and UDP, operate at Layer 3 (Network
Layer) and Layer 4 (Transport Layer). In contrast, application firewalls that perform content
filtering operate at Layer 7 (Application Layer).

Figure 10.1: OSI Model
The OSI model helps developers, system idx_1be27768 engineers, and architects understand how
communication flows between idx_532d4fab an end user and an application. It also helps when deciding
where different security protocols and controls should be implemented across the networking
stack.
The following table illustrates which service you will consume and what layer of the OSI model
it operates at:

Route53/DNS Layer 7
Load Balancers Layer 7
Security Groups Layer 3/4
VPC networking Layer 3

Connecting Elastic Load Balancers to VPC resources
Amazon Load Balancers are idx_9485a29d deployed within your VPC and distribute traffic across multiple
resources, such as EC2 instances. You can configure the load balancer to support various AZs
within the region and define whether it is internet-facing or internal-facing. The key differences
between the two options are as follows:
Internet-facing ELBs: Accept inbound traffic idx_d3a5091a from the internet and distribute it to
resources deployed in either public or private subnets
Internal-facing ELBs: Handle traffic idx_c004c222 originating from within your VPC, such as from
resources in public subnets, and distribute it to resources located in private subnets

To ensure that a load balancer can receive traffic, it's essential to set up its security group with
appropriate inbound rules. These rules must define the port, protocol, and source from which
the traffic is permitted. Additionally, the security groups attached to the target instances must
allow incoming traffic from the load balancer. This is typically achieved by specifying the load
balancer's security group ID as the source in the targets' security group rules.
AWS offers four types of idx_d60db1c3 elastic load balancers, which are discussed in the following
subsections.
Application Load Balancer
AWS Application Load Balancers (ALBs) operate at the application layer (Layer 7) and are
specifically designed to route incoming client traffic based on content using the HTTP and
HTTPS protocols. ALBs support distributing traffic to a variety of targets, including EC2
instances, containers, and AWS Lambda idx_8ae4816c functions. As illustrated in Figure 10.2 and Figure 10.3,
you can deploy these targets across multiple AZs, helping to ensure high availability and fault
tolerance in the event of an AZ failure.
Some key benefits of ALBs idx_13d0edc9 include the following:
Support for path-based routing, allowing idx_fa77c61f you to forward requests based on the
Uniform Resource Locator (URL) in the request
Support for host-based routing, enabling you to forward requests to specific targets
based on the host portion of the URL
•
•
281 High Availability, Fault Tolerance, and Elasticity on AWS
Support for routing requests to multiple applications running on the same EC2
instance using different port numbers
Support for registering Lambda functions as targets, as well as containerized
applications
An ALB includes a configuration idx_ec9e0b80 component called a listener, which defines how incoming
requests are routed to registered targets. Listener rules consist of a priority, conditions, and
actions. When the conditions of a rule are met, the corresponding action is executed. You also
specify the protocol and port used to connect to your targets within the listener configuration.
The targets that receive routed requests are idx_2929e43b defined within target groups. An ALB can have one
or more target groups, which can consist of EC2 instances, IP addresses (for containers), or
Lambda functions. You can also route traffic to targets located outside your VPC.
This flexibility in routing to idx_65ef09cf multiple target groups allows you to create complex routing
architectures for different components of your application. For example, for an e-commerce
website, one target group can route traffic to servers hosting your corporate pages (e.g.,
www.mycompany.com), while another target group handles the e-commerce section (e.g.,

In addition to defining listener rules to route traffic to appropriate targets within a target
group, ALBs also perform health checks on those targets to determine whether they are in a
healthy state. Only targets that respond successfully to these health checks receive traffic. Any

target that fails to respond is idx_9b7a9592 marked as unhealthy and is excluded from the target group. This
ensures that the ALB routes client requests only to healthy targets, helping prevent users from
encountering errors such as "Page cannot be found" or similar messages.
Next, you will learn about the AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB).
Network Load Balancer
Network Load Balancers (NLBs) operate at Layer 4 of the OSI model and can handle millions
of requests per second. NLBs are idx_e343d8ad designed to load balance TCP and UDP traffic while
maintaining ultra-low latencies. A key feature of NLBs is their ability to preserve the source IP
address, allowing backend servers to see the original client IP—an essential requirement for
specific applications.
NLBs also support both static IP addresses and Elastic IP addresses, the latter allowing you to
assign a fixed IP per AZ. Unlike ALBs, NLBs do not inspect application-layer content, meaning
they are unaware of cookies, content types, or custom headers.
Just like ALBs, NLBs perform health checks on registered targets and only route traffic to
targets that are in a healthy state.
Some key benefits of NLBs include idx_86ff1cbb the following:
Ability to handle highly volatile workloads and millions of requests per second
Support for static IP addresses and one Elastic IP address per subnet
Ability to register targets by IP address, including targets outside your VPC (e.g., on-
premises resources)
Support for routing traffic to multiple applications running on the same instance using
different ports
Support for containerized applications, such as those running on Amazon ECS
NLBs are particularly well-suited idx_6dfe944f for high-performance, low-latency workloads, making them
ideal for use cases like gaming, live streaming, and high-frequency trading.
In the next section, you will learn more about Gateway Load Balancers.
Gateway load balancer
Gateway Load Balancers (GWLBs) help idx_c31d3b1d you deploy, scale, and manage third-party virtual
appliances, which are typically purchased from the AWS Marketplace. These appliances are
commonly used for tasks such as security inspection and traffic analysis for idx_3deafa18 data entering and
leaving your VPC. Examples idx_00c2e73d include third-party firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS),
and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS).
•

As shown in Figure 10.5, traffic entering idx_380213a8 your VPC is first routed to these virtual appliances by
the GWLB. The traffic is inspected, and if it passes the checks, it is then forwarded to backend
resources such as EC2 instances hosting your application. If the traffic does not meet the
inspection criteria, it is dropped, and the backend resources are unaware of the presence of the

chunks.heading: Chapter 10 282

appliance in the traffic path.
Figure 10.5: GWLB redirects traffic to the IPS device for inspection before forwarding to backend resources
GWLBs operate at Layer 3 of the OSI model idx_e283f2c0 and provide a single entry and exit point for all
traffic directed to idx_a77b40d9 these services. The load balancer uses a protocol called GENEVE (Generic
Network Virtualization Encapsulation, over port 6081) to send traffic to and from the
virtual appliances.
You will learn about the Classic Load Balancer next.
Classic Load Balancer
The Classic Load Balancer (CLB) is a previous-generation idx_aac98cd3 load balancer that can handle
traffic at both Layer 4 and Layer 7 of the OSI model. However, it offers significantly fewer
features compared to ALBs and NLBs.
AWS recommends migrating any existing CLBs to either ALBs or NLBs, depending on your use
case, unless you have applications running in the EC2-Classic network that cannot be migrated
due to specific constraints.
CLBs can handle HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, and idx_72b85d17 SSL traffic and distribute incoming application traffic
across multiple EC2 instances in multiple AZs.

Chapter 10 284
While load balancing helps improve high availability and distribute traffic across multiple
resources, such as EC2 instances, you still need a mechanism to scale those resources based on
demand automatically. That brings us to the Auto Scaling service, which provides this
capability and is going to be covered in the following section.
Scaling EC2 workloads with AWS Auto Scaling
One of the biggest challenges in deploying software solutions is effectively managing demand.
Before the advent of virtualization idx_40e19568 and cloud technologies, companies would cater to
unexpected demand by following the concept of peak load provisioning. This involves
allocating idx_8bcdd4b6 extra compute and infrastructure idx_b1efa213 resources based on the maximum expected
demand (or peak load) rather than typical usage. This is like investing in a bus with 50 seats
just because once a year, all 50 might be needed, even if most days only 10 people ride it.
With peak load provisioning, you ensure customer satisfaction and system stability during
traffic spikes such as Black Friday sales or product launches. However, for most of the time, the
extra capacity remains underutilized, leading to higher fixed and operational costs.
AWS offers auto scaling capabilities for its idx_a3501ddc core services, enabling you to benefit from
dynamic load provisioning. In this idx_984d7ba7 model, resources scale out or scale in based on actual
demand, making it a far more cost-efficient approach:
Scaling out involves provisioning additional resources, such as extra EC2 instances, to
accommodate an increase in demand
Scaling in means terminating unwanted resources because demand is low
Auto scaling is a regional service that idx_878ec8b7 allows you to scale across multiple AZs within a given
region. This not only helps idx_35a364f1 manage unexpected demand but also ensures high availability in
the event of an entire AZ outage. Auto scaling automatically provisions additional resources
when demand crosses the specified thresholds you define. If demand drops below a defined
threshold, auto scaling can terminate unnecessary resources, ensuring efficient resource
utilization and cost optimization.
In Figure 10.6, two additional EC2 instances were added to the fleet across AZs eu ‑ west ‑ 2a and
eu ‑ west ‑ 2b due to an increase in average CPU utilization exceeding 80% for more than 15
minutes.
•
•
285 High Availability, Fault Tolerance, and Elasticity on AWS
Figure 10.6: Auto Scaling Group responds to a CloudWatch alarm and launches additional instances
Auto Scaling performs idx_ac6cde3d scale-out or scale-in operations based on the threshold idx_00d6ed80 values and
scaling policies you define. In this diagram, the auto scaling service has been configured to
scale out if the average CPU utilization of the fleet exceeds 80% for 15 minutes or more.

chunks.heading: Chapter 10 284
chunks.content:
Amazon CloudWatch is an AWS service that monitors idx_7d912009 and reports on a wide range of metrics,
enabling you to assess the health of your resources. These metrics include CPU utilization, disk
read/write operations, and network idx_52e2c969 bytes in/out. Amazon CloudWatch is discussed in more
detail in Chapter 16.
In the coming sections, you will learn idx_8bf2b14c more about some of the core components of the Amazon
auto scaling service.
Auto scaling groups
When configuring auto scaling for idx_03c8e540 your fleet of EC2 instances, you define an Auto Scaling
group. This group manages all instance launches, terminations, monitoring, and scaling
operations based on your specified configuration. You'll need to provide the following settings:
Minimum number of EC2 instances: This is the lowest number of EC2 instances that
must always be running in your fleet. AWS ensures that the instance count does not fall
below this value.
•

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 10 286
chunks.content:
Chapter 10 286
Desired number of EC2 instances: This represents the optimal number of instances
you want running at any given time. AWS strives to maintain this desired capacity. If
that's not possible (e.g., due to resource limitations), AWS will ensure that at least the
minimum capacity is maintained. Note that the desired capacity can be equal to the
minimum capacity.
Maximum number of EC2 instances: This is the upper limit on the number of EC2
instances in your fleet. The auto scaling service can scale up to this number in response
to increased demand, but will never exceed it. This cap helps prevent runaway scaling
due to application bugs or malicious activity, reducing the risk of service disruption or
unexpected costs.
The auto scaling service launches and terminates EC2 instances based on the scaling policies
you define, the monitored metrics, and any alarms that are triggered. Auto scaling can also
respond when an instance fails a health check, automatically replacing the unhealthy instance.
You can use either the EC2 health checks on their own or combine them with the ELB health
checks (as discussed earlier) to determine the health status of an instance.
The following section outlines the idx_1e80fbbd different scaling policies you can define.
Auto scaling policies
AWS provides several scaling policies that you can configure for your auto scaling groups.
These policies determine when and how your idx_c1e06e8c EC2 instances scale in or out. The available
options include:
Maintain current instance levels: You can configure your auto scaling group to
always maintain a consistent number of EC2 instances across multiple AZs. If an EC2
instance fails, auto scaling automatically replaces it to preserve the desired fleet size.
Manual Scaling: You can manually adjust the minimum, desired, or maximum
number of EC2 instances in the group. Auto Scaling will automatically make the
necessary changes to match your updated settings.
Scheduled Scaling: You can schedule scaling actions to launch or terminate EC2
instances at specific times. This is useful for predictable workload changes, such as
scaling up on Black Friday for e-commerce demand or increasing capacity on the last
Tuesday of the month to support payroll processing.
Dynamic Scaling: When demand is unpredictable, dynamic scaling automatically
adjusts capacity in response to real-time metrics. It initiates scale-out or scale-in
actions in response to threshold breaches. For example, if average CPU utilization
exceeds a defined level for a set duration, auto scaling adds more instances. If
utilization drops below a specified threshold, it removes instances to optimize costs.
•
•
•
•

287 High Availability, Fault Tolerance, and Elasticity on AWS
Dynamic scaling includes three types of policies:

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 10 286
chunks.content:
Target Tracking Scaling Policy: This policy adjusts capacity to maintain a
specific target metric. For example, if your team determines that 45% average
CPU utilization delivers optimal performance, auto scaling will automatically
add or remove instances to keep utilization at that level—ensuring a balance
between performance and cost.
Step Scaling: This method utilizes a predefined set of steps to adjust capacity
according to the extent to which the metric exceeds the threshold. Larger
breaches trigger more significant scaling actions.
Simple Scaling: This type of policy increases or decreases capacity based on a
single scaling metric and a cooldown period after each action.
Predictive Scaling: This policy uses machine learning to forecast future traffic trends
based on historical usage idx_3b6627ab and scheduled actions. It proactively adjusts capacity ahead
of time, ensuring your application is ready for upcoming demand spikes.
When setting up your auto scaling groups and scaling policies, you must specify how the
service should provision your EC2 instances, such as the operating system to use, any software
applications to install, and specific configurations to apply at launch. To do this, you need to
define a Launch Template, which is discussed in the next section.
EC2 launch templates
To set up your auto scaling group, you must configure idx_d0c5ee97 a launch template. This template defines
how your EC2 instances will be provisioned. For example, you must idx_01ebdba7 specify:
An Amazon Machine Image (AMI)
Instance type
Key pair
Security groups
Block device mappings (if needed)
You can also assign IAM roles to the instance profile to grant permissions for AWS services,
such as enabling your application running on EC2 instances to upload and download objects
from an S3 bucket or update a DynamoDB database table. Additionally, you may include
startup scripts that run when the instance idx_9ecfb7e4 launches. This process, known as bootstrapping,
allows you to execute custom scripts written in Bash (for Linux) or PowerShell (for Windows).
Within the user data section of the idx_ff93df64 template, you can script the installation of tools, libraries,
software, utilities, and more.

Now that you have a solid understanding of high availability, scalability, and the tools used to
build a resilient and elastic architecture, the following section introduces a few additional
services that are important for the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner exam. These services are
also included in this chapter because they will be used in the capstone project later.
Supporting application delivery with AWS Secrets
Manager and Amazon SES
AWS offers more than two hundred services, all idx_5a3448a6 designed to help you build resilient, reliable,
scalable, and cost-effective solutions. This chapter introduces idx_059efe55 you to two additional services
that you must learn about to prepare for the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner exam. The
services introduced in this section are also part of the architecture design for your first
capstone project for Belly Brew Co. Limited.
AWS Secrets Manager
AWS Secrets Manager is a fully managed service designed to help you securely store and
access secrets, such as database idx_a1ad366a credentials, access keys, API keys, and other sensitive
information that must be protected.
The service allows you to store sensitive data in an encrypted format, which can only be
accessed by entities with appropriate permissions. Access to these secrets is provided via API
calls, enabling your application to retrieve them at runtime as needed programmatically. This
is a far more secure approach than hardcoding secrets in plain text within your application
code.
For example, if your application needs to update a backend database, it must first authenticate
using a set of credentials. Instead of hardcoding these credentials in plain text within the
application code and increasing security risk, the application can dynamically retrieve them
from Secrets Manager at runtime. This ensures that sensitive information is not stored in plain
text within the source code.
AWS provides additional tools for storing and managing sensitive data, such as environment
variables and API keys, like AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. However, AWS Secrets
•
•
•
•
289 High Availability, Fault Tolerance, and Elasticity on AWS
Manager offers a key advantage: it allows you to automatically rotate sensitive credentials,
such as Amazon RDS usernames and passwords, at defined intervals.
This feature utilizes an AWS Lambda function to automatically rotate credentials and update
the associated database with the new values, much like you would regularly update your

chunks.title: awscertifiedcloudpractitionerclf-c02certificationguidesecondeditio
chunks.heading: Chapter 10 288
chunks.content:
username and password. This automated rotation significantly enhances security by reducing
the risk of credential compromise.
Customers can still use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. This service is ideal when you
simply need a secure, centralized repository to store configuration values like environment
variables and API keys without the need for automatic credential rotation.
Amazon Simple Email Service
Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) is a cloud-based tool that enables you to send
high volumes of email directly from idx_c04ffa20 your applications. Whether you're delivering transactional
messages, promotional campaigns, or newsletters, SES helps you reach a large audience
efficiently. It offers flexible deployment options, allowing you to choose from dedicated,
shared, or custom IP addresses. Plus, with built-in reporting and analytics, you get valuable
insights into email performance and deliverability.
While understanding the theory behind these AWS services is essential for the Cloud
Practitioner exam, hands-on experience is what truly sets you apart in the real world. In the
next section, you'll get the chance to build a complete, end-to-end solution for Belly Brew Co.
Limited. This project brings back the business scenario from Chapter 1 and gives you a practical
opportunity to apply what you've learned in your first capstone project.
Project 10 – Architecting and deploying Belly Brew
Co. Limited's marketing campaign website
In Chapter 1, Belly Brew Co. Limited defined its initial requirement for a customer-facing
website to promote the company brand to idx_c16297cf the public. A key functionality of this requirement
was to gather the contact details of existing and potential customers for use in marketing
campaigns.
To encourage customers to share their idx_bc97c148 contact details, the marketing team has decided to offer
a free e-book on gut-friendly recipes, along with the promise of regular product trials and
discount coupon giveaways. Belly Brew Co. Limited's internal development team would build
the website, but your role as a Cloud Practitioner is to design and architect a solution on AWS
to host that website. Critical to this solution is ensuring that the website is highly available,
scalable, and secure.

8.9 297 High Availability, Fault Tolerance, and Elasticity on AWS
Under Listeners and routing, ensure that the Protocol is set to HTTP, with Port set to
80. Select the target group you created earlier (bb ‑ target ‑ group) from the drop-down
in the Default action section
Scroll to the bottom of the webpage and click the Create load balancer button
Your application load balancer idx_ce32ccf6 will now be created. This will take a couple of minutes, and you
should see the Status as Active as per the following screenshot in Figure 10.11:
Figure 10.11: Application Load Balancer active status
Your application load balancer is now ready. Later, when you configure the auto scaling group,
the service will register your EC2 instances to the target group, and the load balancer will
distribute incoming traffic to those instances.
In the next project task, you will create a secret in AWS Secrets Manager to store and manage
the Amazon RDS database credentials. This will be used by your application to dynamically
retrieve those credentials when accessing the backend database.
Project task 10.3 – Creating a secret in AWS Secrets
Manager
In this project task, you will create a idx_5f914ab8 secret to update and manage your Amazon RDS MySQL
credentials. You will also configure a rotation policy to update the credentials every seven days.
From the top search bar on the AWS management console, search for and navigate to
AWS Secrets Manager
Ensure that you are still in the London region
On the AWS Secrets Manager webpage, click the Store a new secret button
On the Choose secret type webpage, select the option Credentials for Amazon RDS
database

Chapter 10 298
Next, in the Credentials section, provide the database username and password you
configured when you created Belly Brew Co. Limited's database in Chapter 9
Scroll down and in the Database section, select Belly Brew Co. Limited's Database
(bellybrewdb) as per the following screenshot in Figure 10.12:
Figure 10.12: Belly Brew Co. Limited's database
Click Next
Provide a name for your secret in the Secret name and description section. For
example, you can name your secret bb ‑ db ‑ secret
Scroll a bit further down the webpage and click Next
Click the toggle switch to turn Automatic rotation on in the Configure automatic
rotation section
Next, in the Rotation schedule, ensure that the Schedule expression builder is
selected
Set the Time unit to Days and the Days to 7
Scroll down to the Rotation function section. Here, provide a name for your Lambda
rotation function, for idx_7fdfa698 example, bb ‑ rotation. AWS Secrets Manager will add a prefix
to the name with the word SecretsManager. Note that the function name, including
the prefix, must be a maximum of 64 characters. This Lambda rotation function,
created by AWS, is responsible for updating the database credentials. It will also update
the secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
Ensure that Single user is selected as the Rotation strategy
Next, click Next
Scroll to the bottom of the Review webpage and click the Store button
AWS will store the secret bb ‑ db ‑ secret. It will take a few minutes to configure the rotation
settings. After a few minutes, you can refresh the page and then click on the secret name,
bb ‑ db ‑ secret. You will note the Secret details as per the following screenshot in Figure 10.13:
